# Acosta Matos / RIC / hotel-investment poster and perimeter-map continuity — 1 September 2026

**Status:** repo-only continuity and correction record. This record does **not** publish or replace a rendered website route and does not itself establish any criminal, tax, ownership or causation conclusion.

## Purpose

This record preserves the direction developed in the originating ChatGPT thread so that the work is reconstructable after chat deletion. It controls the next corrected poster/infographic and the accompanying 2017–2026 Acosta Matos / RICPE / Canarian Hospitality hotel-investment map.

The working visual direction is a high-contrast public-interest **spoof advertisement** using black/yellow/white/red, organised around: (i) Sun Park / MYND Yaiza as the historical anchor; (ii) the later hotel, RICPE, Canarian Hospitality, MYND, Sholeo and franchise/investment network; (iii) a capital/incentive “flywheel” to be tested rather than assumed; and (iv) a final panel headed **Questions, not conclusions**.

## Mandatory correction rules for the next poster

1. **Do not use approximate names.** Resolve legal persons through CAEPR / the canonical entity controls and preserve trading names, hotel names and brands as separate object classes.
2. Correct “Mind Hotels” to the public brand spelling **MYND Hotels**.
3. Correct “Canary Hospitality” to **Canarian Hospitality, S.L.** where the legal company is intended.
4. **Radisson** is a brand/franchise relationship unless a source separately establishes asset ownership. A Radisson-branded property must not be labelled Acosta-owned merely because Canarian Hospitality manages it or Acosta Matos built/refurbished it.
5. **Sholeo Lodges** is a Canarian Hospitality brand. The user-literal “Solano” has not been positively resolved to a relevant Acosta/Canarian hotel or entity in the finite public-source scan; retain it only as an unresolved literal, with Sholeo as a possible intended candidate, until a source or user clarification resolves it.
6. The exact legal company is **ACOSTA MATOS INVESTMENTS, SOCIEDAD LIMITADA** (plural “INVESTMENTS”), registered on sheet GC 61953. The Acosta Matos Sholeo Maspalomas project page currently prints the source literal “Acosta Matos Investment, S.L.”. Keep that wording only as a labelled source literal; do not use it as the canonical legal denomination.
7. Do not collapse **Construcciones Acosta Matos, S.A.** into the five 2023 demerger beneficiaries. The 6-Nov-2023 total demerger created Grupo Acosta Matos, S.L.; Promociones Acosta Matos, S.L.; Construcciones Acosta Matos, S.L.; Grupo Patrimonial Acosta Matos, S.L.; and Hotel Callao Adeje, S.L. Separate historical acts before and after that structural change.
8. Preserve the existing repository distinction between **RIC (Reserva para Inversiones en Canarias)** and **RIC Private Equity Investment Partners, S.C.R., S.A. (RICPE)**.
9. The words **investor**, **subscriber**, **taxpayer** and **RIC materialiser** are not automatic synonyms. RICPE itself describes a model connecting Canary entrepreneurs/professionals seeking to materialise RIC tax savings with investment opportunities. The poster may question who bore economic risk and who obtained tax benefits, but must not state that a lawful RIC participant is “not an investor” merely because the investment has tax consequences.
10. “Tax avoidance/evasion”, “fraud”, “criminal scheme”, “fruit of the forbidden tree” or equivalent formulations are not to be stated as adjudicated fact. Where retained rhetorically, identify them as attributed allegations, investigative hypotheses or questions and preserve the strongest lawful alternative explanation.

## Controlling fifth question

The additional bottom-panel question is preserved as:

> **WHO WERE THE “INVESTORS” — INDEPENDENT CAPITAL, RIC TAXPAYERS/SUBSCRIBERS, INTRODUCED CLIENTS, RELATED PARTIES, OR INTERMEDIARIES?**

The evidential sub-questions are: who actually bore economic risk; who obtained the RIC/tax benefit; who subscribed; who introduced whom; who was paid for introduction, placement or structuring; what conflicts/abstentions applied; and where the subscribed/borrowed/public-supported money ultimately went.

## Unitary reverse-engineering hypothesis — preserved with proof boundary

The project-side hypothesis to test is whether Sun Park was used, from the pre-reopening / 2017–2018 period onward, not merely as a hotel asset but as a platform of asset/control credibility, promotional material, investor access, RIC materialisation, refinancing, operating income and transaction momentum from which later economic benefits or further asset acquisitions could have been generated.

That hypothesis must be tested through a traceable sequence rather than converted into a conclusion by repetition:

`Sun Park access/control/title state` → `project/investor representation` → `RICPE/other financing` → `works / HNT / MYND` → `cash/equity/debt/guarantee/fee flows` → `later assets or projects`.

For each downstream hotel/project, test actual provenance: acquisition consideration; equity subscriber; lender; RICPE or other financing; intercompany balances; guarantees/collateral; construction margin; management/brand fees; public incentives/aid; refinancing; distributions; sale/exit proceeds; and any documented recycling into later projects. **Chronology or group affiliation alone is not tracing.**

The phrase “fruit of the forbidden tree” can therefore remain only as a rhetorical investigative metaphor: the evidence question is whether a particular downstream asset or benefit is financially traceable to a proved unlawful antecedent. No such chain is presumed by this control.

## Material corrections established in the 1-Sep-2026 scan

### Radisson Blu Lanzarote

Do **not** depict as an Acosta-owned hotel on present evidence. Public and RICPE material identifies **Las Coronas de Teguise, S.L.** as owner/project company, Canarian Hospitality as manager, Radisson as the brand, and RICPE as financier. Public Teguise/industry reporting identifies the Al-Bochi family as the owners/investors. Acosta Matos can be represented separately where a source establishes rehabilitation/construction work.

### Sholeo Lodges Los Gigantes

Do **not** depict as a presently proved Acosta-owned hotel. Public project material identifies **Oceánica Hotel Management, S.L.** as property/acquisition vehicle and Canarian Hospitality as manager. BORME does, however, establish a historical perimeter connection: Oceánica was previously unipersonal, Laura Patricia Acosta Matos was sole administrator, and on 30-Nov-2022 it lost unipersonal status; she ceased and Aeromédica Canaria, S.L. became sole administrator. The exact subsequent shareholding is therefore a registry/open-proof question, not a basis to call the hotel wholly Acosta-owned.

### Radisson Resort & Residences Tenerife / former Parque San Antonio

The asset company is **Tenerife Assets Company, S.L.** Public reporting describes the 25-Jul-2024 acquisition from HIP by a group of Canary investors, with Canarian Hospitality managing and Acosta Matos undertaking architecture/construction/renovation. BORME proves a material governance connection: Grupo Patrimonial Acosta Matos, S.L. served on Tenerife Assets Company’s board and as secretary until the April-2025 governance change. That supports a perimeter/co-investor-governance node but **does not establish an exact Acosta equity percentage**. Exact shareholder/equity tracing remains open.

### Acosta Matos Investments, S.L.

BORME establishes incorporation on 30-Nov-2023, sole shareholder Construcciones Acosta Matos, S.A., sole administrator Laura Patricia Acosta Matos, sheet GC 61953. A January-2024 capital increase took subscribed capital to €10.633m. This is a priority tracing node for Sholeo Maspalomas and any other assets assigned to it.

### Hotel New Trend, S.L. / MYND Yaiza

The Acosta Matos project page identifies Hotel New Trend, S.L. as owner of MYND Yaiza. BORME records the earlier CAM→HNT Sun Park tourist-unit segregation and, in June 2024, identifies **Grupo Patrimonial Acosta Matos, S.L. as HNT’s sole shareholder**. This is a stronger post-2023 ownership bridge than the draft poster used and must replace generic “Acosta Matos” ownership wording.

## Platform chronology to retain

- **2017–2018:** Sun Park / LPB debt, property and control-material period already reconstructed in the repository; 2018 is not to be treated as the start of every relationship if earlier evidence exists.
- **2019:** RICPE registered; José Daniel Acosta Matos is a RICPE board member from the documented 2019 period.
- **2020–2021:** AC Tenerife and MYND Adeje financing/development; broader RICPE relationship and investor-process period.
- **2022:** MYND Yaiza / HNT and Radisson Blu Lanzarote RICPE financing; Sun Park tourist-unit segregation into HNT; openings of MYND Yaiza and Radisson Blu Lanzarote.
- **2023:** Sholeo Los Gigantes; Acosta Matos corporate demerger; incorporation of Acosta Matos Investments.
- **2024:** Las Palmas Sholeo flats; Tenerife Assets / former Parque San Antonio acquisition by investor group; RICPE Sholeo Maspalomas investment; HNT sole-shareholder change to Grupo Patrimonial Acosta Matos.
- **2025:** Sholeo Maspalomas; Canarian roadmap reference to MYND Marieta; Radisson Resort & Residences Tenerife / former Parque San Antonio reopening path and RICPE financing.
- **2026:** new 97-suite five-star Playa Blanca development announced as Grupo Acosta Matos + Canary investors, with Canarian Hospitality and a planned Radisson relationship; south-Fuerteventura/Jandía pipeline remains a separately announced future project whose exact asset/SPV must be resolved.
